searches.query: new data science tools and frameworks
searches.answer: The sources mention several newer data science tools and frameworks. Cleanlab is a versatile tool that works with various classifiers and has specific workflows for tasks like token classification and outlier detection. Optimus can use multiple data engines and supports various data formats. Polars offers a performance boost over Pandas for DataFrames. Spacy provides pre-trained models for NLP tasks and has an easy-to-use API. Streamlit simplifies the creation of interactive data science applications and dashboards. Apache Arrow's in-memory columnar format accelerates data processing and supports scalability across distributed systems. TensorFlow is highlighted for its use in deep learning architectures. Scikit-learn and Keras are also noted for their machine learning capabilities. Additionally, tools like Altair RapidMiner, Alteryx One, Amazon SageMaker, and others are mentioned for their roles in data science workflows.

searches.query: latest research papers AI ML simplified
searches.answer: The latest research papers in AI/ML include "SimCLR" from February 2020, "Idefics2" from April 2024, "Phi 3 Vision" from May 2024, and "PerceptionLM" from April 2025, all available on GitHub. Morgan Stanley's research includes "Rethinking Langevin Thompson Sampling" and "Average-Case Hardness of Parity Problems." Towards Data Science highlights "Small Language Models are the Future" by Belcak et al. from 2025. GeeksforGeeks lists "Attention Is All You Need" as a must-read, along with other foundational papers. YouTube's deep learning monitor recommends checking for hot and fresh papers for real-time updates.
